semantics.function: sel=0 selects all eight bits of a; sel=1 selects all eight bits of b
semantics.timing: Pure combinational selection, no clock or cycle latency, no stored state
semantics.reset: No reset port or reset behavior
semantics.initialization: No initialization required; output follows current inputs
semantics.unknown_select: Use standard SystemVerilog conditional-operator bitwise merge for X/Z select

numeric.data: Unsigned eight-bit bit patterns, preserved exactly
numeric.arithmetic: None; no rounding, saturation, extension, truncation, or overflow

verification.oracle: For each known select, independently compare each output bit to the corresponding selected input bit
verification.coverage: Exhaust all 256 a values, 256 b values, and both known select values; exercise X/Z select with matching and differing bits
verification.tools: Icarus Verilog v12, explicit dev_tb top, -g2012, finite compile and simulation timeouts
verification.static: Check port widths, purely combinational driver, absence of state and simulation-only DUT constructs

specification_ambiguities: The example declares scalar out despite describing an 8-bit mux. Treat this buggy declaration as requiring correction to out[7:0].
The problem does not specify X/Z select behavior; standard conditional operator merge semantics are used.
